title: Cold rebuild: Simulate a liveness probe
summary: Rebuild Simulate a liveness probe from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Simulate a liveness probe** in *Liveness, readiness and startup probes*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Your liveness probe calls `/health`, which checks the database. The database has a 30-second outage. What happens?
options: Every replica fails liveness and is restarted, turning a short DB blip into a full outage and restart storm
Pods are removed from the Service until the DB returns, then come back
steps.explain: Liveness should check only the process itself. Put dependency checks in **readiness**, and even there be careful: if all replicas go unready at once, the Service has no endpoints.

steps.title: Rebuild Simulate a liveness probe cold
prompt: Write `List<int> Restarts(bool[] results, int periodSeconds, int failureThreshold)`. `results[i]` is the outcome of the probe at time `i * periodSeconds`. Return the times (in seconds) at which the container is restarted. After a restart, the failure count resets to 0.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
List<int> Restarts(bool[] results, int periodSeconds, int failureThreshold)
